commits.message:
Rebuild a deposit-trace block whose end passed before its commit

A resumed deposit-trace journey keeps the deposited block it prepared before
the stop. When the run resumes after that block's end, the commit's validity
range is inverted and its script evaluation fails while the transaction is
built, so neither the expiry rebuild nor the late-refusal path is reached.
The fixture's commit now settles such a block as expired before building,
and the existing loop rebuilds it with a fresh end time.

Settle a header commit refused past its validity bound as expired

The journey fixture fixes a block's end time when it prepares the block, and
the commit's validity ends there. When the predecessor's DA attestation ran
past that end, the commit was built already expired; the node refused it with
Ogmios 3118 and the actor raised a submission error, so the fixture's
rebuild-on-expiry path never ran and the watcher journey failed. A refusal at
or past the upper bound is now an expiry: the transaction is in no mempool,
so the caller rebuilds the block. A refusal before the lower bound stays a
submission error.

Match lucid-evolution 0.8 Data.to in the iterative Plutus Data encoder

lucid-evolution 0.8 encodes Plutus Data with a pure JavaScript encoder first and falls back to CML only when that encoder declines. The JavaScript encoder keeps the last of a map's entries with equal keys before it encodes any value, so a value that a later key replaces is never checked; CML serializes every key and value before replacing, so it refuses the same tree when a replaced value cannot be encoded. The iterative encoder modelled only CML and refused trees that Data.to now accepts (the differential test's seed 426, a map with two equal keys whose replaced value carried a constructor index above 2^64 - 1).

The encoder now plans the tree under the JavaScript encoder's rules (number or bigint constructor index, Array fields, keys planned first and only surviving values planned) and, if that refuses, under CML's rules as before. Edge cases cover both outcomes: a replaced bad value accepted, and the same tree refused when another feature (a string or object index, Set fields) sends Lucid to CML. The edge table moves to its own module to keep the test under the line cap.

Re-pin the contract registry and fix two CI reds from the final batch

The contract registry digests in midgard-contracts.test.ts moved with the tighter event-history admission and the correction lock's ADA top-up; both pins are re-taken from the current blueprint (the same values CI computed).

process.process-mpfs.ts shrank to 1537 lines when the duplicate-outref refusal became in-order classification, so its module-size cap is lowered to match.

devnet-stack-service-preflight.test.ts compared the compiled profile's literal name with "local-devnet-testing", which fails to typecheck when another profile is compiled (CI builds preprod-testing). The name is widened to string before the comparison.

Regenerate the blueprint-bound fixtures and fit ledgers after the correction-lock merge

The correction-lock rule and the admission changes reached this branch on
separate lines, each with its own regenerated outputs; the merge kept the
admission side. This regenerates the DA deployment fixture, the watcher
initialization fixture and the two transition-trace fit ledgers once against
a fresh preprod-testing blueprint of the merged tree, through their
`contrib artifacts sync` channels.
Merge the chain-rule withdrawal value checks into the L1 follower branch

Judge withdrawal values by the chain's rule in the node and the prover

The node classified a withdrawal's requested value against the ledger output
by comparing re-encoded CBOR, and counted lovelace toward the 100-asset cap.
The withdrawal-mistag family judges by step-03's rule instead: the ADA policy
holds exactly the empty name, lovelace is equal, the non-ADA assets match as a
set, and at most 100 non-ADA assets are counted (lovelace excluded). An output
with exactly 100 non-ADA assets was therefore tagged TooManyTokensInWithdrawal
by the node and valid by the chain. The prover's own comparison also ignored
extra names under the ADA policy.

withdrawal-value.ts now holds that rule once; the SDK classifier (used by the
block producer, foreign replay and the validation replay) and the
withdrawal-mistag prover both use it. The SDK already writes withdrawal values
with bytewise-sorted keys, which admission requires; tests pin that.

Tests: node classification cases for out-of-order policies sent as raw CBOR,
mixed-width names, missing and extra assets, a second ADA name, and 100/101
non-ADA assets; 12 Aiken vectors through step-03's `output_value_matches_v1`
with a TypeScript twin asserting the node agrees on each; withdrawal-mistag
cases at the cap; admission emulator rows for SDK-built values. No validator
hash changes.
Merge trace-order classification of duplicate-outref withdrawals into the L1 follower branch

Classify duplicate-outref withdrawals in trace order instead of refusing the block

Two admitted withdrawal orders may name the same L2 outref, and admission
does not compare orders with each other. When both fell in one block window,
block building failed with "multiple withdrawals target the same L2 outref",
every tick, on every operator: overdue withdrawals are forced into the next
block, so the same pair was selected again and block production stopped.

The producer now classifies a block's withdrawals in trace-step order, each
against the ledger the earlier payable ones leave. The first payable order
drains the outref; a later order on it finds no output and is tagged
NonExistentWithdrawalUtxo. This is what foreign-block replay, the validation
replay and the withdrawal-mistag family already derive, and the double-
withdraw family refuses a block whose second leaf is non-payable.

Tests: trace-order unit cases; a Postgres-backed processMpfs build of two
orders on one outref whose block the verified-block-import replay accepts
(and refuses with the duplicate re-tagged valid); withdrawal-mistag emulator
in both polarities on that block, the honest one refused at step 04; Aiken
regression pins for the NonExistentWithdrawalUtxo tag in double-withdraw
steps 01 and 02 (no validator hash changes).
Merge declared-order contrib tests into the L1 follower branch
Merge the dev-ex leftovers into the L1 follower branch

Merge the correction-lock ADA top-up rule into the L1 follower branch

Regenerate the blueprint-bound fixtures and fit ledgers for the correction-lock rule

The correction-lock validator changed, so its script hash and every hash parameterized by it moved. Regenerated with each channel's generator against a fresh preprod-testing blueprint (artifacts sync, which also ran each channel's check): the DA contract deployment fixture, the watcher user-event initialization fixture, and the transition-trace forced-window and workflow fit ledgers. Fit-ledger budgets moved in both directions (at most about 0.19M memory units per row, signed bytes +22 at most); no row spends the correction lock.

Refs #648

Prove a correction tops up a lock funded only for Idle (#648)

Seeds the real correction lock with exactly the ledger minimum for its Idle datum, as a lock minted outside atomic initialization is, then runs a prune (Idle to Locked) and the terminal removal (Locked to Idle) through the applied validators. The prune output carries more ADA than the Idle lock and the release keeps it. Under the old strict value equality the prune is refused on chain.

Refs #648

Correct the correction-lock funding note at initialization

The note said a correction preserves the lock's value and that a top-up is forbidden. A correction may now add ADA to the lock, so the Locked-size funding at initialization is a choice that spares the first correction a top-up, the same choice the state-queue root makes a few lines below. No behavior changes.
